verdict: The four scripts do what their specs say on every tested behaviour: 91 tests pass, 0 fail, 8 are skipped because they need the app. 26 mutations were tried and 21 were caught. The 5 survivors are test gaps: the record sha re-check in compare, the blind order's dependence on the plan hash, the audit's epoch binding in gate, the sample sd and the context-fall filter for g in cost. There are no high findings. There are 14 medium ones: 2 code defects in compare (an unbound attempt gives tokens 0 instead of transcript-missing; the scorer result is not checked for completeness), 1 race and 1 liveness fault in compare, 4 design or spec gaps (an approval is not bound to the draft's content, a hazard can be rewritten under its old id, G1-G12 are never required, the blind order can be computed from public values), 3 test-gap findings for the 5 surviving mutations (the blind-order survivor is folded into the blind-order gap), 2 fail-open reads in cost (an unchecked card read, the default inputs path) and 1 brief that tells the S1 session it is the control.

tests.command: node tools/lane.mjs --label review-U5 --timeout-s 300 -- node --test --test-concurrency=1 tcb/test/<protocol-freeze|compare|gate|cost>.test.mjs (one file per lane call)
tests.output_tail: protocol-freeze: tests 28, pass 26, skipped 2 (NA1, NA2); compare: tests 24, pass 22, skipped 2; gate: tests 24, pass 22, skipped 2; cost: tests 23, pass 21, skipped 2. Every skip is a test that needs the app.

findings.claim: An attempt with no session whose folder has no transcript, and a task that has no row, add 0 tokens and are not marked missing. The arm's tokens, confirmed_per_extra_million_tokens and prediction.actual come out too low, and the check line says pass.
findings.evidence: Only the a.session branch sets missing (line 303). In the a.folder branch, an empty transcriptsForFolder result, or an exception it swallows (lines 309-313), leaves files empty with missing false. rows.get(task) undefined gives no attempts and no flag. The spec says a missing transcript gives tokens null and reason transcript-missing:<task>, and every task row has a folder (CONTRACT section 3.6).
findings.fix: Set missing = true when a row is absent, and when an attempt has neither a session main transcript nor any folder transcript. Fall back to the folder when a session's main transcript is absent, as cost.mjs discover does.

findings.claim: The ledger, the plan binding, the certificates and the commit records are read before run.lock is taken. Under the lock, comparison.json and a check line are written without checking that the ledger has not moved. A protocol-amend of the analysis plan, or a new certificate, that lands in between gives a 'descriptive, n = 1 per arm' file bound to a superseded plan sha, and its check line follows the amend in the ledger.
findings.evidence: loadLedger and bindPlan run at line 732-733 with no lock. withRunLock at line 776 re-reads the ledger only to find the previous check line (line 779). Nothing compares the head seq or hash with the snapshot the figures came from. CONTRACT 2.1 asks for facts before the lock, but the write is not re-validated.
findings.fix: Keep the ledger head (seq and hash) of the snapshot. Under the lock, re-read the head. If it changed, return exit 75 (or recompute once) and write nothing. Do the same in anon before creating the key.

findings.claim: The scorer's result is not checked for completeness. Leaving out items, or guessing an arm not in arm_names, still gives status 'scored'. rate is computed over the items returned (n_items = scores.length), and an arm with no score gets rubric_total null.
findings.evidence: Line 444 rejects only unknown or duplicate items. Nothing compares seen.size with Object.keys(keyItems).length, and guess_arm is never checked against the key's arm names. The scorer brief demands 'exactly one entry per item in index.json'. A scorer that answers only the item it is sure of gets rate 1/1 = 1.
findings.fix: After the loop, if seen.size !== Object.keys(keyItems).length, or any guess_arm is not one of the key's arms, return invalid() (status not_run, reason scores-invalid). Add test cases for both to T13.

findings.claim: The blind order can be computed from values that are not sealed. The seed is sha256('blind:' + plan_sha256): the plan sha is in the ledger and in plan/frozen/, the arm names are in views/blind/index.json, and lib.rng is public. The coordinator profile reads plan/ and views/ and runs Bash, so the sealed key adds no secrecy. Mutation CM7, which made the seed independent of the plan hash, also survived, so T3 does not pin what the spec states.
findings.evidence: Line 669 is const seed = lib.sha256hex(`blind:${bound.sha256}`). The key file records rng_seed. coordinator.json read_prefixes include {root}/plan/ and {root}/views/, with bash tcb-node. CM7 left all tests passing.
findings.fix: On the first anon, draw the seed with crypto.randomBytes(32) and store it only in sealed/blind/<sha12>.json. On later runs, read the seed from the existing key so a repeat stays byte-identical. The spec line 'order depends only on the plan hash' needs the same change. In T3, assert that two plan hashes give different orders for a fixed four-arm set.

findings.claim: If anon runs while only some arms are committed, it creates the exclusive key for that plan sha. Every later anon, once the remaining arms are committed, exits 1 blind-key-differs, and exit 1 is not among compare's exit codes. The missing arms can then never be blinded under that plan, and score keeps using the partial key.
findings.evidence: live holds only the committed arms (line 665). The key is created exclusively and never replaced (lines 758-761). A different item set gives the 'blind-key-differs' exit 1 at line 751. The spec's exit list is 0, 2, 3, 64, 66, 70, 75.
findings.fix: Refuse anon with exit 2 (reason arms-not-committed) unless every arm in arm_tasks has a committed review. Equivalently, include the sorted arm set in the key name and check it in score.

findings.claim: Mutation CM3 survived: removing the comparison of the object with the commit record's sha256 broke no test. A commit record whose outputs[].id was swapped for another valid object of the same kind (its bytes still match its own name) goes undetected by the tests.
findings.evidence: T16 edits object bytes only, and getObject already catches that through the name check. With line 125 disabled, all tests passed.
findings.fix: Add a T16 case: rewrite store/commits/<task>.review.json so outputs[0].id names a second, valid review object, and keep the old sha256. Expect exit 3 object-mismatch.

findings.claim: The owner's approval is bound to subject and quote text only, not to the draft's content. The coordinator can edit a draft after the owner approved it, keep approval.quote unchanged, and the first freeze accepts the edited draft as owner-approved (R33, R39).
findings.evidence: The owner line format is {act, subject, quote} (CONTRACT line 378), with no hash. found (lines 357-359) compares kind, act, subject, clip500(quote) and seq. For a first freeze, after = 0, so any earlier approve line with the same quote serves.
findings.fix: Have status.mjs owner --act approve record the sha256 of the canonical draft shown to the owner, and have protocol-freeze require it to equal the sha256 of the draft it freezes (approval-unrecorded otherwise). This is a contract change (owner line gains sha256).

findings.claim: Design R55 says gate passes only if 'every high hazard (gaps G1-G12 included) is covered or accepted'. The gate requires only P1..P21 in p_ids. A mapper that leaves G1-G12 out of the hazard list therefore passes, and the gaps never need cover or the owner's acceptance.
findings.evidence: Line 341 loops i = 1..21 over 'P' only. The design's lines 517-518 and 599-612 define G1-G12 as completeness-analysis rows of the problems table.
findings.fix: Also require G1..G12 in some hazard's p_ids (slug p-id-missing, listing them). Better, read the required id list from the problems table that is handed to the mapper. Fix the spec line too.

findings.claim: The append-only check looks only at whether parent hazard ids are still present. A child hazards object can keep h3 and rewrite its statement or severity, and an earlier owner accept line for hazard:h3 then covers a hazard the owner never saw. The spec says changes go through a new id with supersedes.
findings.evidence: dropped (line 331) collects only parent ids that are absent from the child. accepted (lines 347-349) is a set of subjects from every owner accept line, whenever it was written and whatever text it covered.
findings.fix: For each parent hazard, require the child's entry with the same id to keep classical_name, statement and severity equal (only status, covered_by and p_ids may change); otherwise add hazards-not-append-only. Alternatively, bind the accept to the hazard's canonical sha.

findings.claim: Mutation GT7 survived: removing the epoch match from the audit lookup broke no test. A clean audit of another epoch (for example epoch 1, when epoch 2's analysis is the committed one and read the full design) would clear analysis-tainted, and no test would notice.
findings.evidence: With line 283 reduced to l.kind === 'audit' && l.task === c.row.task, T5 and T12 both passed.
findings.fix: Add a T12 case: commit stpa at epoch 2, with a clean audit line for epoch 1 only (expect exit 2 audit-missing), and with a tainted epoch-2 line followed by a clean epoch-1 line (expect exit 1 analysis-tainted).

findings.claim: Card objects are read with lib.readJson straight from store/objects, without getObject's name check and without comparing against the commit record's sha256. Unreadable commit records and cards are dropped silently. A changed card (its question_ids, for example) shifts t_q and k_q, which admission later reads (R47). A lost record moves a task into 'unattributed' with no reason saying why.
findings.evidence: Line 717 reads lib.readJson(path.join(root,'store','objects',`${id}.json`)), and the catches at lines 699-701 and 719-721 swallow every error. The spec reads 'store/commits/* and, through them, card objects', and CONTRACT treats bytes that differ from the name as a tamper.
findings.fix: Read with lib.getObject(root, id) and compare sha256hex(canonicalize(v)) with output.sha256. On any failure, add {task, id, why} to a new 'unreadable' list in the result and set trusted false (exit 2, within cost's exit codes).

findings.claim: Two survivors in the statistics. KC2 (sd divided by n instead of n-1) survived because no test has n >= 2 for a unit. KC3 (context falls averaged into g) survived because T10's median over three sessions [2800, 3000, 3200] hides epoch 1's corrupted mean (-4880). The assertion message says the fall is not averaged, but the test cannot see it.
findings.evidence: Line 478 asserts only sd === null with one task. In T10, the median of [-4880, 3000, 3200] is still 3000. Both mutations left all tests passing.
findings.fix: Add a unit with two tasks of known tokens (for example 100 and 300, so sd = 141.42...). In T10, assert g on a role with one session that contains the fall, or assert the per-session g, so the median cannot mask it.

findings.claim: compute first tries <script dir>/../cost-inputs.json. In the flat layout that is the run root (or tcb-build), outside tcb/, and no single writer owns that path. Any file there silently replaces the owner-approved template tcb/cost-inputs.json.
findings.evidence: Line 1041 is path.join(HERE, '..', 'cost-inputs.json'), checked with existsSync before HERE/cost-inputs.json. The brief says the flat layout is the rule and scripts find their files relative to their own file.

findings.claim: The child brief tells the S1 session that it is the 'control': 'Role `control`: you start no readers...', and line 3 renders role `{{role}}` = control. That reveals the experimental comparison to one of the arms being compared, and spec/briefs.md says no brief mentions that anything is tested.
findings.evidence: child.md line 42. CONTRACT line 298 role enum includes 'control', and the brief prints {{role}} on line 3.
findings.fix: Show the session a neutral label (for example 'solo') in place of the role name, and phrase line 42 as 'If your manifest lists no reader agent type, you start no readers...'. The no-reader rule already comes from the profile's agent_types.

not_findings_checked: McNemar exact p hand-checked: b=2,c=1 gives 2*(1+3)/8 = 1; b=5,c=0 gives 2/32 = 0.0625; code matches.
predict n_cap hand-checked: floor((300000-60000-10000)/2800)+1 = 83; matches T7.
protocol-freeze --file containment (dot-dot, junctions, plan/protocols itself a junction) goes through lib.isUnder with realpath; the 66 comes before any read.
No network call, no process kill and no write outside the run root in the four scripts. The briefs name no model tier and none of the banned words.
cost from-transcripts parses outside run.lock and writes under it, as CONTRACT 2.1 requires; T18 covers this.
